paired_source_controls: Both arms use the same host, compiler, source path, fixtures and capacities. The before arm restores baseline root/target-test manifests and lockfiles; candidate inputs are restored afterwards. Raw proxy report Git metadata names the candidate checkout while the before input snapshot is dirty. Package inputs/source digests and ELF hashes, rather than that raw Git label alone, identify the arms.

standard_measurement_before.boundary: Reachable test workloads, not whole-feature upper bounds. Static RAM excludes stack. Two-role EDHOC and protocol tables use stack storage; this is not a peak RAM measurement.

before.source_digest_boundary: Sorted relative path, NUL, file bytes, NUL for src/**/*.rs, target-tests/src/**/*.rs, both Cargo manifests/lockfiles, target-tests/build.rs, rust-toolchain.toml and tests/fixtures/{i,r}.ccs when present.
before.boundary: Two simultaneous opaque forwards with 1024-byte origin payloads and a public local GET, with plain and secure-capable receiving endpoints and an unsecured outbound endpoint. Origin replies are scripted; this does not establish protected local interoperability or hardware behavior. Endpoints/Shared are static; driver futures, proxy and simulated link are on the measured stack. Endpoint construction precedes painting and its peak is unmeasured. Stack paint is an exercised-write measurement, not a worst-case bound. CPU and physical hardware are not measured.

growth_attribution.method: Sized t/T/r/R symbols, nm --radix=d -C, parsed as decimal and grouped by paths with generic arguments stripped. Anonymous/literal names are excluded from the displayed attribution.
growth_attribution.interpretation: Most added secure-workload code is in P256 field arithmetic: montgomery_reduce+1270, add+318 and sub_inner+278 named bytes in the EDHOC/full fixture. The full dependency refresh was measured as a unit; contributions from individual dependency versions were not isolated. Smaller plain-workload growth also remains visible.
growth_attribution.boundary: Symbol groups are attribution, not additional allocations or independent complete partitions of linked section totals.

boundary: Linked Cortex-M/QEMU reference fixtures, not complete device firmware or a worst-case RAM/stack bound. Selected flash/static section sums retain each tool's accounting; nested futures, task pools and stack are not summed twice. No CPU or constant-time-execution claim follows from functional checks. Applications must refresh their own lockfiles to receive transitive fixes.
